title: t2117: feat(pulse): dispatch throttle on overlapping file footprints — prevent CONFLICTING cascades at source
body:
Follow-up from t2116/GH#19106 systemic fix for worker PR loss via CONFLICTING-close. After landing the update-branch attempt and needs-maintainer-review skip, two remaining loss vectors remain.

## Problem

Multiple workers are dispatched in parallel against the same file (e.g. .agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf ratchet PRs, .agents/workflows/brief/templates.md simplification PRs). Whichever PR merges first invalidates all others. The update-branch salvage path (t2116) now rescues many of these, but some are genuine line-conflicting edits on the same hunk and still cascade through CONFLICTING-close.

## Proposed approach

Introduce a lightweight file-footprint lock in the dispatch path:
- When a brief is parsed, extract its 'Files to modify' section into a canonical file list.
- Before dispatching a new worker for an issue, check the dispatch-dedup ledger for any currently in-flight issue whose file list overlaps. If found, defer dispatch one cycle rather than parallelising.
- Decays after the blocking issue reaches status:in-review or its PR merges.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two issues with overlapping file footprints never have simultaneous dispatched workers.
2. Issues with disjoint file footprints still dispatch in parallel (no over-serialisation).
3. Regression test in .agents/scripts/tests/ that builds a mock dispatch state and asserts the deferral.
4. Log line with (t2xxx) audit tag on every deferral.

## Context

Root-cause data and prior fix: GH#19106 / PR #19107. Relevant files:
- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh (the dedup ledger)
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh (dispatch caller)
- .agents/templates/brief-template.md (Files to modify section format)

title: t2118: feat(pulse-merge): carry forward closed PR diff as worker guidance on linked issue
body:
Follow-up from t2116/GH#19106. When _close_conflicting_pr does have to close a PR for a true semantic conflict, the worker's solved diff is silently discarded and the re-dispatched worker starts from scratch — token waste, and re-produces the same race.

## Problem

Currently, a conflicting-close leaves the linked issue in its original form. The next worker reads the same brief and produces the same diff, hits the same conflict, and the loop repeats.

## Proposed approach

Before closing a CONFLICTING PR, extract its diff via gh pr diff, wrap it in a fenced block, and append it to the linked issue body under a '## Prior worker attempt (PR #NNN, closed CONFLICTING)' section. Idempotent — never append twice for the same PR. The re-dispatched worker reads the diff as work-in-progress and can rebase/apply it instead of re-deriving it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Closed CONFLICTING PR diffs appear on the linked issue body in a clearly marked section.
2. Idempotent — running the close path twice for the same PR does not duplicate the section.
3. Size-capped — diffs over 20KB are truncated with a '... (truncated, full diff at PR #NNN)' marker, so the issue body does not blow up.
4. Does not fire for origin:interactive or needs-maintainer-review skips (those paths never close now, post-t2116).
5. Regression test mirroring test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh pattern.

## Context

Root-cause data and prior fix: GH#19106 / PR #19107. Relevant files:

title: Review followup: PR #18963 — t2091: fix dispatch-dedup self-login bypass + worker closed-issue guard + process docs
body:
## Unaddressed review bot suggestions

PR #18963 was merged with unaddressed review bot feedback. Each comment
below includes its file path, line number, a direct link to the inline
review comment, and a `diff` fence with the code context the bot was
flagging. Resolved and outdated threads are filtered out via GitHub's
GraphQL review-thread state. Read the relevant lines, decide whether
the suggestion is correct, and either apply the fix or close this issue
with a wontfix rationale.

**Source PR:** https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/18963

---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `prompts/build.txt`
section 6a). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

#### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call

Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply:
the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside
what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision
